change: Grid sweep of 1728 constant sets: normalisation {ratio_to_max, minmax, zscore} x publisher_discount {0.8..0.95} x publisher_confidence {0.5, 0.75, 1} x shrinkage_weight {1, 2, 3} x context_bonus {0, 0.03, 0.06, 0.1} x family mix {flat, three fixed mixes}. 183 sets reach tau >= 0.8. Mean tau by setting: minmax 0.741 vs ratio_to_max 0.701 vs zscore 0.676; coding-heavy family mix (0.6/0.15/0.25) 0.757 vs flat 0.688; the other constants move mean tau by under 0.02. Chosen region: minmax with the coding-heavy mix, where 122 of 144 neighbouring sets give tau >= 0.8 (min 0.782, median 0.818), so the result is not a knife-edge fit. Picked the region's centre (discount 0.85, confidence 0.75, shrinkage 2, context 0.03), not its maximum (0.891).
disagreements: Absolute cut-offs no longer fit the minmax scale: LongCat-2.5 fell to Tier 2 and six Tier 2 models to Tier 3. Next: cut-offs as a share of the top score.
